questions.q: State the basic properties of a magnet.
answer: A magnet shows several definite properties.

answer.text: It attracts magnetic materials such as iron, nickel and cobalt, but not non-magnetic materials like wood, plastic or paper.
Every magnet has two poles, north and south, and its pulling force is strongest at the poles. The poles always exist in pairs — breaking a magnet gives smaller magnets, each with both poles.
Like poles repel each other and unlike poles attract; repulsion is the sure test of a magnet.
A freely suspended magnet always comes to rest in the north–south direction.

questions.q: How does a magnetic compass work, and how can a magnet be made?

answer.text: A compass contains a small, freely pivoted magnetic needle. Because a freely suspended magnet always settles in the north–south direction, the needle points north, letting us find directions. This works because the Earth itself behaves like a giant magnet.
An ordinary iron bar can be turned into a magnet by stroking it many times in the same direction with one pole of a bar magnet, lifting the magnet away at the end of each stroke.
Magnets lose their power if heated, hammered or dropped, so bar magnets are stored in pairs with unlike poles together and kept away from electronic devices.
